title: RunPod REST v1 -> v2 migration (v1 returns 410 Gone on 2026-11-15)
description:
HARD DEADLINE 2026-11-15: RunPod retires REST API v1; every call returns 410 Gone.
GraphQL (api.runpod.io/graphql) follows in early 2027. Source: Runpod Weekly #35
(2026-09-16) + the v1-to-v2 migration guide at docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/migrate-from-v1

This breaks the ENTIRE remote-engine feature for any SHIPPED version still on v1,
including installs that never update. The migration must ship in a release with enough
runway for users to auto-update (target: shipped by 2026-11-01).

Scope - routes/runpodRemote.js is the only client (const REST at line 33, 13 call
sites through _rest()):
  - base rest.runpod.io/v1 becomes api.runpod.io/v2
  - auth unchanged (Bearer)
  - POST/GET /pods, GET/DELETE /pods/{id} become /v2/pods; LIST now wraps the array as
    {"pods":[...]} instead of returning a bare array
  - POST /pods/{id}/start and /stop COLLAPSE into POST /v2/pods/{id}/action with the
    action in the body. No v2 equivalent for reset.
  - /networkvolumes x4 (list, create, delete, PATCH grow) renamed, {id} standardised
  - POST /templates renamed
  - create spec goes NESTED: gpu settings under `gpu`, storage under `mounts`
  - errors move to RFC 9457 {title,status,detail} from {message}. _reason() in
    routes/remotePodLifecycle.js:783 already reads detail/title, so it is half-covered.

Also check at migration time:
  - v2 adds catalog browsing, which is the replacement for the GraphQL half
    (client.gpuTypes / client.availability) before GraphQL dies in early 2027.
  - Global Volumes (beta, 0.09 USD/GB/mo plus passed-through read/write/file-op costs)
    mount a volume in ANY data center, which would remove the volume DC-lock documented
    at routes/remotePodLifecycle.js:797. Cost-check before adopting: our hot-store
    re-reads 30-80GB of weights per Pod start. Separate decision - do not block the
    migration on it.

Testing needs a real Pod (real money) - see docs/runpod-remote-engine.md.

UNVERIFIED: the email claims every v1 response already carries a Sunset header. An
unauthenticated probe of rest.runpod.io/v1/pods on 2026-09-17 returned 401 with NO
Sunset header. Do not build a detector on that claim without checking with a real key.

Calendar backstop: an all-day reminder on 2026-10-22 asks whether this has shipped.
